entries.title: Valley of Achor
entries.description: A ruin and a flight of steps in the Valley of Achor.
entries.evidence: Late-antique tradition puts Achor north of Jericho, beside Galgala (Onomasticon). On PEF Sheet XVIII Wadi Nuweiʿimeh rises at springs NW of Jericho and runs to a lower course NE of it. Whether TIR’s “Achor Vallis” label means this valley is unverified; its gazetteer page is unread.
entries.caution: The Iron Age Achor tradition points toward the Buqeia. No reported ruin-and-steps combination decides between them.
entries.landmark: a ruin; steps
entries.period: No feature dated. Valley only: Early Roman houses and a stepped cistern on the south bank, a late Hellenistic tomb on the north bank (Taha 2020 pp. 277–278)
entries.sources: Milik DJD D4 p. 263; SWP III p. 226; ʿAtiqot 41 (Aronshtam) pp. 91, 99

entries.title: The monument
entries.description: A monument and a course of masonry.
entries.evidence: The editions disagree on the third datum: a third masonry course (Puech 2015 p. 29), a third gravestone (Lefkovits 2000 p. 50) or a personal name (Milik 1960 pp. 139, 144). The entry names no place; Puech groups it with entry 1, and the Kidron monuments are kept as funerary monuments.
entries.caution: Zechariah’s monument is monolithic and Absalom’s lower body is rock-cut, so neither supplies a built third course (Kloner–Zissu 2003 pp. 142, 146). This excludes that branch only; the gravestone and name branches are untested. No monument is identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The great courtyard
entries.description: A cistern, a courtyard and a colonnaded space.
entries.evidence: Milik puts the peristyle court in the Temple (DJD pp. 272–274); Puech queries the Valley of Achor (2006 p. 175). Under the Temple platform, tank No. 8, the “Great Sea”, is the largest cistern (SWP Jerusalem pp. 219–220). The project proposes it as a possible match, low.
entries.caution: Tank No. 8 is undated and lies under the southern outer court, while Milik’s peristyle is the inner court. No cistern is reported in relation to a peristyle court. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The mound of Kohlit
entries.description: A mound, a water conduit and a rock cleft or bath of immersion at Kohlit.
entries.evidence: Tell es-Sultan supplies the mound: its main city was early, so it was an old ruin-mound by the 1st century (SWP p. 223). Channels run from the spring below it but are undated (SWP pp. 222–223).
entries.caution: No rock cleft or immersion installation is reported at the tell; the dated Hasmonean–Herodian baths and aqueducts lie in the palace area to the south (Eshel pp. 99–100). Koḥlit remains unidentified; Tell es-Sultan is Puech’s hypothesis.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The winding stair

entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The title follows Puech’s reading, a spiral staircase; the Text tab shows Milik’s letters, read as a foundry. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.

entries.title: The Millo cistern
entries.description: A cistern and steps at a place interpreted as the Millo or an esplanade.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The title follows the Esplanade reading of the same word at III 8 and III 11; here Puech (2015 pp. 38–39) and Lefkovits (pp. 103–104) read a salt pit below the steps, and the Text tab shows המלח, ha-Melaḥ. No repository record says why the entry was placed in the Tyropoeon. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.

entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The title follows Puech’s “house of Tribute” (2015 pp. 38, 40); he rejects the sense “measure”. The Text tab shows המדח, translated “Washing(?)”. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index

entries.title: The courtyard cistern
entries.description: An underground chamber or tower in a courtyard, with a cistern in it.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The eastern gate
entries.description: A cistern with a channel opposite the eastern gate.
entries.evidence: Milik and Puech take the gate as the Temple’s East Gate (Puech 2006 p. 184). Warren records many undated rock-cut cisterns with feed channels under the platform (Recovery pp. 204 ff.).
entries.caution: On Warren’s Plate VI no recorded cistern lies 19 cubits (8.5–10 m) from the Golden Gate; the nearest, No. 15, is 30 m away. Only open mouths were recorded and deep debris lies before the gate, so a buried cistern is not excluded. The 1st-century gate is known only from texts.
entries.landmark: a cistern with a channel, opposite the gate
entries.period: not stated

entries.title: The eastern wall
entries.description: A cistern beneath a wall, beside a rock spur and threshold.
entries.evidence: Warren describes rock scarps and the masonry of the east wall and its south-east angle (Recovery pp. 135–141, 153–158), and undated cisterns with channels under the platform (pp. 204 ff.).
entries.caution: No report describes a cistern under the east wall with a threshold. Whether the wall is the city’s or the Temple enclosure’s is open (Lefkovits p. 130). The placement follows entry 9 (Puech 2006 p. 184); the individual feature has not been identified.
entries.landmark: a cistern under the wall; a rock spur; a threshold
entries.period: not stated

entries.title: Kohlit's pool
entries.description: A corner of a pool associated with Kohlit.
entries.evidence: On Puech’s hypothesis this is a pool east of Tell es-Sultan. The SWP records a shallow reservoir, 24 × 40 ft, at the spring on the tell’s east foot (via Dorrell 1993 p. 96).
entries.caution: The basin’s construction and early use are undated. The present reservoir was built in 1898 (Dorrell p. 111), so that branch fails the period. No northern corner is identified. Koḥlit itself is unlocated.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.

entries.description: A cistern and a pillar at Kohlit.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.

entries.title: The entering conduit
entries.description: A conduit and a pool approached on entering; the location needs restoration.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The pool is Puech’s restoration, “to the po[ol]” (2015 p. 48). He rejects Eshel’s restored “Hyrcania” as too long for the gap (p. 50 n. 193). The Text tab leaves the conduit’s goal unread. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Achor's two features
entries.description: Two features in Achor, read as cavities, tamarisks or buildings by different editors.
entries.evidence: Caves in the cliffs bordering Wadi Nuweiʿimeh were in use in the 1st century BCE–1st century CE (Aronshtam pp. 98, 101; Eisenberg p. 120; Sion pp. 80–81). Under Puech’s “cavities” reading the project tests one pair, V/49 and its neighbour V/48.
entries.caution: The Text tab shows הכיפין, translated “domes(?)”, which matches none of these three readings. No source reports a pair of cavities, tamarisks or buildings. The period shown is for the Nuweiʿimeh caves: the Buqeia has only Iron Age ruins (period fit earlier only; Phase 5 check low). ʿAin Duk is kept only as the springs at the head of the same valley; nothing specific to it is recorded.
entries.landmark: two cavities (Puech) / tamarisks (Milik) / buildings (Lefkovits)
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE (Nuweiʿimeh cliff caves)
entries.sources: ʿAtiqot 41 (Aronshtam pp. 98, 101; Eisenberg p. 120; Sion pp. 80–81)

entries.title: Asla
entries.description: An earth pit in the area called Asla.
entries.evidence: The name survives as Wadi el-ʿAṣla / Gofet el-ʿAṣla (Milik DJD D6; SWP III p. 200). Red marl, which suits an “earth” or “red” pit, is common there (Puech 2015 p. 52 n. 206).
entries.caution: No pit is reported, the wadi’s archaeology is unpublished and no period is stated. The IAA escarpment survey reports Early Roman caves but does not name ʿAṣla (Yitah et al. pp. 180–185). Lefkovits reads no place name. The rating rests on the surviving name and entry order.
entries.landmark: an earth pit
entries.period: not stated
entries.sources: SWP III p. 200; Milik DJD D6; ʿAtiqot 41 (Yitah et al.) pp. 180–185

entries.title: The Kohlit pit
entries.description: A pit associated with Kohlit.
entries.evidence: North of Tell es-Sultan Kenyon records a Roman cistern (N.S.1), a hewn pit with Roman sherds (P29) and later quarry pits (Kenyon II pp. 539–544; III p. 174).
entries.caution: These are generic pits. None is identified as the eastern pit of a set, and N.S.1 has no plan. The quarry pits cut the 1st-century graves and have no absolute date. Koḥlit is unlocated; the placement depends on entries 4, 11, 15 and 60.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Valley of Sekakah
entries.description: A cairn or dam in the valley of Sekakah.
entries.evidence: A cairn and a dam imply different features. Puech prefers a cairn; the dam proposal must be checked independently.
entries.caution: The proposed Qumran dam is reconstructed. Neither it nor a particular cairn has been established as this entry’s landmark.
entries.landmark: a cairn (Milik, Puech) or a dam (Eshel)
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Eshel CSS pp. 94–95; SWP III p. 210; ʿAtiqot 41 (Baruch et al.) pp. 197–198; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026)

entries.title: Sekakah
entries.description: The head of a water conduit associated with Sekakah; the link and stone landmark are partly restored.
entries.evidence: Qumran’s water system supplies a plausible conduit-head setting. Ilan–Amit’s 1989 plan puts the visible intake beside a reconstructed dam. Stacey (2007) dates the main aqueduct after the 31 BCE earthquake and makes the dam and the cliff tunnel a later stage.
entries.caution: The link to Sekakah and the stone noun are partly restored. Northern approach and northern side must be tested separately. Under Stacey’s phasing, the earlier channel began where the aqueduct leaves the cliff, so the head of a construction stage is an alternative to the dam intake; the phasing is a hypothesis. The pin marks the settlement.
entries.landmark: the head of a water conduit
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Eshel CSS pp. 94–95; ʿAtiqot 41 preface p. viii; Milik DJD D9; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026); Lefkovits 2000 pp. 185–189; Stacey 2009, The Dam; Stacey 2007, DSD 14 pp. 222–243

entries.title: Solomon's reservoir
entries.description: A fissure in Sekakah east of a reservoir associated with Solomon.
entries.evidence: Qumran’s reservoirs provide a setting to test against the fissure east of the named reservoir.
entries.caution: Neither the ancient reservoir name nor the specific eastern fissure has been established. Jerusalem’s similarly named pool does not relocate this entry.
entries.landmark: a fissure; a reservoir ("of Solomon")
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Cohen & Porat, HA-ESI 132 (2020); Milik 1960 p. 147; SWP III p. 210; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026)

entries.title: Solomon or Shallum’s channel
entries.description: A trench or channel associated with Solomon or Shallum, directed toward a large landmark read as a boulder or mound.
entries.evidence: Puech allows Shallum as an alternative to Solomon and a large boulder as the landmark. The channel’s connection to entry 22’s reservoir is conditional.
entries.caution: No origin or endpoint is identified for the stated distance. Entry order alone does not establish a continuous route.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026)

entries.title: The Kippa ravine
entries.description: A tomb in the Kippa ravine, on the approach from Jericho toward Sekakah.
entries.evidence: The wording permits a regional approach test from Jericho toward Sekakah. Wadi Kuteif remains a published proposal.
entries.caution: The recorded rock-cut chamber is undated and does not identify the required tomb. The only dated tombs recorded in the wadi, four pit tombs with glass beads (WBADB E508), are Early Islamic. A route from entry 23 to entry 24 is not specified.
entries.landmark: a tomb
entries.period: chamber undated; pit tombs in the wadi Early Islamic (WBADB E508)
entries.sources: SWP III p. 220; Milik DJD D12; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026)

entries.title: Cave of the Column
entries.description: A cave entrance distinguished by a column.
entries.evidence: The existing IV/17 assessment documents two openings and a rock-cut dividing pillar at Jebel Abu Saraj. The northern member lies on the right of Sion’s Plan 5 after orienting its north arrow. Qumran remains a separate site-level proposal.
entries.caution: IV/17 is a provisional comparison: its aperture normals point southeast, and threshold, wall phase, ancient floor and digging origin are unresolved. Twin Cave, about 1 km north of Kh. Qumran, is the only cave matching every clause at both-mouths level (Bar-Adon 1989), but its mouth positions and date are unknown. It and IV/11 remain controls; the form is not unique.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon; Sion 2002, ʿAtiqot 41 pp. 61–64, Plan 5 p. 63; existing IV/17 assessment (2 October 2026)

entries.title: The facing cave
entries.description: A cave, its entrance and an adjacent mound or clod.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index

entries.caution: Puech reads משכן as the queen’s “mausoleum” (2015 p. 60), and the Text tab translates “resting place”; the files name no editor for the dwelling sense. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.

entries.title: The high priest's ford
entries.description: A cairn at a crossing associated with the high priest.
entries.evidence: Not reported.
entries.caution: The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.landmark: a cairn at a ford
entries.period: not stated
entries.sources: SWP III p. 170

entries.title: The collected waters
entries.description: A conduit, a reservoir and a collection of water; Jericho appears in a restoration.
entries.evidence: Two conditional tests are complete; both are inconclusive. At Jericho, the northern of the two early Hasmonean pools (about 18 × 13 m) does not stand out from the southern control in the offset test. At Hyrcania, the northern member of the double pool (Patrich 1989 p. 255) has no fixed measuring origin. ʿAin Duk and Tell es-Sultan have no entry-29 test.
entries.caution: The title follows Puech’s restoration, a collection of the waters (2015 pp. 62–63); the Text tab leaves the word damaged (קי◦) and restores no Jericho. Jericho is restored, and Hyrcania rests on Eshel’s Qi[dron], which Puech finds too long for the gap. At Jericho the original inlets are lost and Herod joined the two pools. At Hyrcania the pool’s inlet is unidentified, and Patrich dates its abandonment after Herod. No deposit point is proposed.
entries.period: Tested pools Hasmonean (Jericho 103–67 BCE, joined under Herod; Hyrcania, abandoned after Herod)
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon; Trümper 2018 pp. 280–286; Netzer 1983 pp. 101, 105–106; Patrich 1989 pp. 255–256, Fig. 22; Patrich 2002 p. 336; entry-29 assessments (2 October 2026)

entries.title: House of Haqqoz
entries.description: A cave next to the cool room of a house associated with Haqqoz.
entries.evidence: Puech proposes an estate of the priestly family Haqqoz at Jericho (2015 p. 66). The district has palace baths and pools, and cliff caves used in the 1st c. BCE–1st c. CE (Eshel CSS pp. 99–100).
entries.caution: No house of Haqqoz, cool room or adjacent cave is identified, and the estate and cave chronology is unestablished. “Cool room” is Puech’s restoration; Milik reads “in its vicinity”, and several editors read “summer house”, not a family name. The placement is district-level.
entries.landmark: a cave next to a cool room of a house
entries.period: district in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE; estate and cave undated
entries.sources: Eshel CSS pp. 99–100; Puech 2015 pp. 36, 101

entries.title: Doq
entries.description: A corner at Doq, read as a fortress or as a drying floor.
entries.evidence: A Hasmonean fortress occupied the summit, supplied by a wadi diversion, a 500 m channel and nine cisterns. The name Doq survives nearby at Ain Duk.
entries.caution: Editors disagree over “guard post” and “drying place.” The 2026 plate check leans to the drying place, so the fortress is not the landmark by default. The surviving name does not distinguish the summit from the spring; Q24 remains open. Garbrecht and Peleg note that Doq was apparently not rebuilt by Herod, so first-century use of the summit is not shown.
entries.landmark: the corner of a fortress (Milik) or a drying floor (Puech)
entries.period: Hasmonean fortress; later use not shown; required feature undated
entries.sources: Eshel CSS pp. 92, 100–101; Milik DJD D19; SWP III p. 205; ʿAtiqot 41 (Eisenberg p. 120); Garbrecht & Peleg, BA 57 (1994) pp. 164–165

entries.title: Koziba
entries.description: A water outlet and a retaining wall at Koziba.
entries.evidence: Choziba preserves a related name, attested from the 5th-century monastery. The Wadi Qelt aqueducts were built under the Hasmoneans and Herod and used in the period (Eshel CSS pp. 97–100). SWP describes a channel head at ʿAin Qelt, a division at Jisr ed-Deir and a cliffside wall opposite Deir el-Kelt.
entries.caution: No outlet with a wall at its mouth is recorded in the Qelt. The outlet’s function is unresolved and the wall’s period is not established. Lefkovits reads “of Buz”, and הטור may mean a wall, parapet, mountain or rock. The pin represents a stretch of the valley.
entries.landmark: a water outlet; a retaining wall
entries.period: Qelt aqueducts in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE; outlet and wall undated
entries.sources: Eshel CSS pp. 97–100; SWP III pp. 205–206, 227–228; Milik DJD D20

entries.title: Ahiyah's treasury
entries.description: A conduit, a treasury and a road; the personal name is disputed.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The title follows Puech’s house of the treasury and Aḥiyah (2015 p. 69). Milik reads place names (Bet Ḥaṣor, Ḥazor), Lefkovits reads Ahim, and the Text tab shows אחור, “Aḥor”. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The inscribed stone
entries.description: A valley marked by an inscribed stone.
entries.evidence: The public site index keeps three candidates, in Jerusalem (Bir Ayyub), the Jericho district and Doq. No inscribed stone or other stone marker is reported at any of them.
entries.caution: The title follows Puech’s and Lefkovits’s engraved inscription (Puech 2015 p. 69); the Text tab shows other letters, translated “in the middle of the ◦”. “The outer valley” is unnamed. The three candidates follow entry order, not a name or feature argument. At En-Rogel the survey records only an undated well. The placement remains at site or district level.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Kidron
entries.description: A cairn at the mouth of the Kidron gorge.
entries.evidence: The Kidron gorge supplies the named landscape; Mar Saba and Hyrcania feature in published proposals.
entries.caution: “Mouth of the gorge” could also describe the escarpment exit, and no cairn is reported. Hyrcania’s link needs יגר to mean “dam” (Luria, Eshel), which Puech rejects (2015 p. 73 n. 298). Eshel’s system description names no southern dam (CSS p. 95), but Patrich records southern intake station 1 (1989 p. 244); its position and date are unknown.
entries.landmark: a cairn at the mouth of the gorge
entries.period: no cairn reported; Herodian aqueduct passes this stretch (Eshel CSS p. 95); other remains Byzantine or later
entries.sources: SWP III pp. 3, 219; ʿAtiqot 41 (Dahari) pp. 233, 239

entries.title: Valley of Shaveh
entries.description: Fallow land and an underground chamber in Shaveh.
entries.evidence: Second Temple rock-cut tombs are reported in the Kidron valley in general (Avni & Greenhut 1996, abstract only). They are generic underground chambers.
entries.caution: No source fixes which valley the Shaveh is (Q22): Puech looks toward Beth ha-Kerem, Milik to Bethso at the Baqʿah. No north-facing chamber is identified, and “fallow land” cannot be tested. The label position is schematic.
entries.landmark: fallow land; an underground chamber
entries.period: valley unlocated; Kidron tombs of the period (abstract only)
entries.sources: Avni & Greenhut 1996; SWP III pp. 53–54

entries.title: Shaveh's irrigated land
entries.description: Irrigated land and a chamber or stone marker in Shaveh.
entries.evidence: Partly (irrigated gardens below siloam, undated).
entries.caution: The title follows Milik’s and Puech’s reading ברוי, irrigated land; the Text tab shows בדור, translated “enclosure”. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.landmark: irrigated land; a chamber or cippus
entries.period: not stated
entries.sources: Wilson 1871 pp. 21–22; SWP III pp. 53–54

entries.title: Netophah
entries.description: A spring associated with a dovecote or cave opening.
entries.evidence: The spring name and the Khareitun setting support a candidate in this district.
entries.caution: The required dovecote, rock opening or tower has not been demonstrated at this spring, and no columbarium is recorded within 2 km. Dated remains there are late antique and medieval. The placement rests on the name ʿAin en-Naṭuf (Milik 1960 p. 150); Lefkovits places Netophah at Kh. Badd Faluh.
entries.landmark: a dovecote (or cave opening) at the spring
entries.period: not stated
entries.sources: SWP III pp. 357–376; Milik 1960 p. 150; Milik DJD C4

entries.title: The terrace
entries.description: An underground chamber facing east in the second terrace; Milik reads a place name instead of the terrace.
entries.evidence: Terraced land by Tekoa, rock-cut tombs, cisterns and caves are reported in the sector (SWP III pp. 296–300). They are generic features; only the Herodium works are dated to the 1st c. BCE.
entries.caution: No chamber facing east is reported, and the sector is chosen by entry order, not by a name. Puech reads “second terrace”; Milik reads a place name, Tekelet ha-Šani, found only in his text. Hirschfeld’s 1985 survey of the area has not been consulted.
entries.landmark: an underground chamber facing east, in a terrace
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Horon or the Horites
entries.description: Burial chambers facing the Sea (west) or south, and a channel; the name and the direction have competing readings.
entries.evidence: Under “facing the Sea” (west), favoured by the 2026 plate check, Beth-Horon keeps Milik’s textual basis, which also needs his article read as “Beth”. The name survives at Beit ʿUr. Rock-cut tombs are reported at both villages; the lower village’s tomb with period pottery faces south (Peleg 2004 Fig. 1). Naṭuf rests on the order of the entries.
entries.caution: Milik himself later judged the Horite tombs near Beit Guvrin slightly more likely; that necropolis is a possible, low candidate that is recorded but not mapped. Puech reads “south”. Jeremias dates the necropolis only as Seleucid. No chamber facing west, channel or 16-cubit depth is reported anywhere.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The damaged entry
entries.description: A very short, uncertain expression. No candidate has a defensible map location.
entries.evidence: The public index leaves this entry unmapped.
entries.caution: The reading and geographical setting remain unresolved.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The sounding conduit
entries.description: A conduit and the sound of water; one reading supplies the name Kephar Nebo.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Beth Tamar
entries.description: A pit, exposed rock and a place read as Beth Tamar.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The exposed rock follows Puech’s “rocky ground” (2015 p. 75), on letters Lefkovits shares; the Text tab reads “at the outlet of the Valley of Peleʿ(?)”. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The fort's upper room
entries.description: A fort, an upper room and a dovecote.
entries.evidence: Puech reads a dovecote in a “small fort”, not a place name (2015 p. 86), and places entries 39–45 near Tekoa and Herodium by their order. Herodium had a fortress with towers (SWP III pp. 330–331), and talmudic texts tie pigeons to this district (Milik C4).
entries.caution: No dovecote is reported in the sector. The Text tab’s “second upper storey” needs three levels; Puech’s reading needs two. In an exploratory review of 179 recorded columbaria none meets the text shown, and only Masada’s towers meet Puech’s reading, through Netzer’s reconstruction. Masada rests on Milik’s emendation (Phase 3: weak or ruled out).
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The ravine cistern
entries.description: A cistern and channels in a ravine.
entries.evidence: ASI 102/486 records an undated ancient well at ʿEn Rogel (Bir Ayyub). In the Tekoa–Herodium sector, cemented cisterns at Tekoa and a reservoir and aqueduct at Herodium are reported (SWP III pp. 27, 330–331). No cistern fed by channels from a great wadi is identified at either.
entries.caution: The entry names no place. Puech’s order puts it in the Tekoa–Herodium sector; the repository records no argument for Bir Ayyub, and the map region follows only the first listed candidate. A well fits only Milik’s wheel-well reading; the water survey left it unscored because its feed is unrecorded.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Beth ha-Kerem
entries.description: A large reservoir at Beth ha-Kerem.
entries.evidence: Ramat Rahel has an earlier pool-and-channel enclosure and later settlement.
entries.caution: The description’s large reservoir follows Milik’s gloss (C70), which has not been rechecked; Puech reads a pool or basin (2015 p. 85), Lefkovits a pool or a deep pit (p. 331). The known enclosure lay under fill containing pottery as late as the second century BCE. The current verdict is low; the required period reservoir remains unverified.
entries.landmark: a pool or basin (Puech, Lefkovits); a large reservoir in Milik’s gloss (C70)
entries.period: earlier enclosure (burial fill includes 2nd-c. BCE pottery)
entries.sources: Lipschits et al., Ramat Raḥel 2006–07 report pp. 15–18; INJ 17 pp. 59–60; HA-ESI 137

entries.title: The spring basin
entries.description: A spring, basin and chamber in a valley whose name is disputed.
entries.evidence: ASI 102/486 records an undated ancient well at ʿEn Rogel (Bir Ayyub). No basin is recorded within 1 km, and no black stone or entrance is reported.
entries.caution: The spring and chamber follow Puech’s “underground (near) its spring” (2015 p. 85); the Text tab reads “on its west side”, as Milik and Lefkovits. Bir Ayyub depends on Puech’s “valley of Job” (2015 p. 89), whose antiquity he says needs checking (n. 392); the Text tab shows Wolters’s “Valley of Zered(?)”, and Lefkovits reads “Pure Valley”.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Absalom's monument
entries.description: A freestanding monument associated with Absalom.
entries.evidence: The standing Kidron monument is dated to the first century CE by its architectural style (Zias 2023; Kloner–Zissu pp. 142–143).
entries.caution: Its earliest surviving labels name Zacharias. A first-century association with Absalom remains unestablished. Its original entrance is in the south wall; the western opening is a later breach (Kloner–Zissu p. 142). The entry asks only for its west side.
entries.landmark: a free-standing monument named for Absalom
entries.period: 1st c. CE, by architectural style
entries.sources: Zias 2023; Høgenhaven p. 79 n. 67; Lefkovits p. 348

entries.title: Siloam?
entries.description: A water installation and a trough; the reading that names Siloam is disputed.
entries.evidence: The tunnel outlet and surrounding pools supply a compatible water-installation setting. Szanton distinguishes the smaller Silwan pool from Birkat el-Hamra.
entries.caution: The title and the water outlet follow Puech’s “spring (?) of Siloam waters” (2015 p. 86); the Text tab shows Milik’s letters, “basin(?) of the bathhouse(?) of Raḥil(?)”. Siloam needs a supplied word; the plates lean to Puech’s waw without deciding it. No period trough is established. Conduit L103 is conditionally excluded as Puech’s hollowed stone and as built before a 69/70 CE coin; Milik’s pipe branch survives.
entries.landmark: a water outlet; pools; a trough
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE (pool/outlet setting); small-pool floor laid in or after 69/70 CE
entries.sources: Szanton 2023 pp. 35–42; Lefkovits pp. 352–354; Puech 2015 p. 92; see site_identification_review.md

entries.title: Zadok's court
entries.description: The four corners of a court associated with Zadok (Puech), an inner court (Lefkovits) or a pool (the Text tab).
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The title and its Hebrew follow Puech’s “courtyard (of the tomb) of Ṣadoq” (2015 p. 139); no other edition reads Zadok at X 17. Lefkovits restores an inner court; the Text tab restores “In the upper pool”, Wise’s conjecture. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Zadok's tomb setting
entries.description: A tomb with a vestibule and pillar, associated with Zadok's surroundings.
entries.evidence: Rock-cut tombs of the Second Temple period are reported in the Kidron generally (Avni & Greenhut 1996, abstract only). Milik places Zadok’s tomb on the west bank below the south-east corner, from texts and traditions (DJD III pp. 270–271). At the angle itself Warren found debris and masonry, no tombs (1871 pp. 135–141).
entries.caution: The only recorded pillared-porch tomb nearby, Bene Ḥezir, stands on the east bank (Kloner–Zissu pp. 143–146). Phase 5 infers that the tomb type fits Jeremias’s east-bank placement better than Milik’s. No tomb is named Zadok. The slope south of the corner was a 1st-century CE refuse dump (HA-ESI 136). Lefkovits reads “ossuary”, not “stoa”.
entries.landmark: a tomb with a vestibule and pillar
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Avni & Greenhut 1996; Milik DJD pp. 270–271; Warren 1871 pp. 135–141; HA-ESI 136

entries.title: The rock opposite Zadok
entries.description: A west-facing rock opposite Zadok's court or garden.
entries.evidence: The Kidron’s east side is a west-facing rock slope with rock-cut tombs (Milik DJD III pp. 270–271; Avni & Greenhut 1996, abstract). At the Silwan necropolis anchor the survey records Iron Age II monuments and kokhim “apparently from the Herodian period” (ASI 102/420).
entries.caution: No source locates Zadok’s court or garden, so “opposite” has no fixed point. No rock with a great slab at its base is recorded; the tomb lane never meets the garden clause. The 1st-century CE monument that Zias dates (Absalom’s Tomb) stands at the Kidron monuments, north of this anchor.
entries.landmark: a west-facing rock opposite Zadok's court
entries.period: tombs of the period in the Kidron generally; at this anchor kokhim only “apparently Herodian” (ASI 102/420)
entries.sources: Milik DJD pp. 270–271; Avni & Greenhut 1996; Zias 2023

entries.title: The gallery tomb
entries.description: A tomb associated with galleries.
entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The title and its Hebrew follow Puech’s “colonnades” (2015 p. 94); the Text tab shows הסכין, translated “rock ‘knife’(?)”. The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: The Jericho people's tomb
entries.description: A tomb associated with people from Jericho.
entries.evidence: Both Jerusalem candidates rest on entry order; no name places the tomb in Jerusalem. Only generic tombs are recorded near either (ASI 102/420; 102/407, 102/424). If the tomb was reserved for priests, Puech names the tomb of the Benê Ḥezîr in the Kidron valley as one possibility (2015 p. 101). That tomb stands at the Kidron monuments, which are not a candidate for this entry.
entries.caution: The title follows Puech’s reading ירחו, Jericho; the Text tab shows טהור, translated “ritually pure”; Wolters, reading from the metal, also found “pure” there. Under the Jericho reading, the regional tomb lane scored Puech’s branch in the Jericho region, not in Jerusalem. No tomb at either candidate fits the owner phrase (54-L, 54-M: 0 matches). No repository source proposes Gethsemane; Allegro put this tomb among the common graves on the Kidron’s east bank (1960 p. 93).
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon; Puech 2015 p. 101

entries.title: House of the two pools
entries.description: A double reservoir with a smaller basin; Bethesda depends on an editorial identification.
entries.evidence: The editors report a double pool at St Anne’s, with a smaller northern basin, in use in the 1st century (John 5:2; Milik DJD III pp. 271–272; Høgenhaven p. 84). They rely on excavation reports not read in the repository (Vincent and Abel 1926; Jeremias 1949/1966).
entries.caution: The smaller basin follows Milik’s and Puech’s reading לימומית; the Text tab reads “on the right”. The text may describe two pools without naming Bethesda; the 2026 plate check shows what looks like a ḥet where Milik’s Bethesda needs a taw. The nearby Strouthion twin pool prevents a unique match on that feature alone.
entries.landmark: a double reservoir with a smaller basin
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Milik DJD pp. 271–272; Høgenhaven p. 84; Warren 1871 pp. 196–197

entries.title: The burial chamber
entries.description: A burial complex with recesses, a cave, entrance stones and a platform.
entries.evidence: The entry names no place. Bethesda follows from the preceding entry and Milik’s “just nearby”; the Kidron candidate follows the burial reading. No burial chamber, cave, platform or cistern tied to this entry is reported at either.
entries.caution: The cave and recesses follow Puech’s restoration and his burial niche (2015 pp. 94, 107); the Text tab leaves the cave unread and reads “the cistern”. West-facing kokhim tombs with several rooms are common. The nearest documented ones, the Jehoshaphat cave and Bene Ḥezir (Kloner–Zissu pp. 140–146), stand at the Kidron monuments, which are not a candidate here. Milik splits the entry into three deposits.
entries.period: No feature dated. Sites only: Bethesda pools in 1st-c. use (John 5:2, via editors); Silwan kokhim “apparently Herodian” (ASI 102/420)
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon

entries.title: Mount Gerizim
entries.description: A step and an upper pit on Mount Gerizim.
entries.evidence: The mountain name provides the geographical anchor. Magen distinguishes the eastern monumental staircase, the southern seven-step flight, the 15-step flight at E1, and the courtyard cistern in Area P building IV. These are separate installations.
entries.caution: The city was destroyed about 110 BCE. A later Hasmonean garrison is reported, but feature-specific use of the stairs or cistern in the scroll’s period remains unverified. Festus specimen K35264 (58/59 CE) is catalogued at P5178, basket 51777; the total of three is a type count, not three coins demonstrated at that locus. Its architectural and deposition contexts remain unknown. No specific step or upper pit is identified.
entries.landmark: a step; an upper pit
entries.period: earlier (standing as ruins) and later; a Hasmonean garrison into the 70s BCE (coins), not tied to these features; stray coins only in the 1st c. CE
entries.sources: Magen, NEAEHL 5 (2008) pp. 1742–1747; Magen et al., JSP 19 (2021) pp. 39–40, 46, 58–59, 104–105, 159; SWP II pp. 187–190; Lefkovits p. 412; Milik DJD p. 274; Magen 2008 plan p. 1743; catalogue-methodology correction (1 October 2026)

entries.title: Beth Sham
entries.description: The mouth of a spring at a place usually compared with Beth Shean.
entries.evidence: Several perennial springs are recorded at Beisan, among them ʿAin el-Melab by the theatre (SWP II pp. 81, 102–107). The town was in use in the period: a dam and pool of the 1st c. BCE–1st c. CE in its farmland (Har’el 2016) and a mausoleum of the later 1st c. BCE (Tzin and Najar 2022).
entries.caution: The scroll’s final mem differs from the usual nun in Beth Shean. No evidence selects the particular spring, and no spring mouth is dated. The dated dam and pool stored water in the farmland; they are not a spring outlet. Milik’s main fountain is known only from 4th–12th-century writers.
entries.landmark: the mouth of a spring
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: SWP II pp. 81, 102–107; Har'el, HA-ESI 2016; Horowitz & Atrash, HA-ESI 2016

entries.title: Bezek?
entries.description: A great conduit; the Bezek reading competes with other readings.
entries.evidence: Zertal identifies Eusebius’s two villages called Bezek, 17 miles from Neapolis, with the two Ibziq sites. A kokhim tomb excavated at Kh. Ibziq in 1971 held pottery of the 1st–2nd centuries CE, which fits Puech’s alternative “burial chamber” reading in type. Zertal places the older Bezeq at nearby Kh. Salhab.
entries.caution: Zertal’s survey reports cisterns and burial caves but no conduit at either Ibziq site, and few Early Roman sherds on the surface. No conduit is reported at Kh. Salhab either. The place name depends on Puech’s reading הבזך, which Allegro and Lefkovits share; the Text tab shows הבור, “the cistern”, the reading of Wilmot and Wise.
entries.landmark: a great conduit
entries.period: partly: Roman kokhim tomb of the 1st–2nd c. CE (HA 40 p. 22); few Early Roman surface sherds (Upper Ibziq: two ER vessels illustrated; Lower Ibziq from Byzantine)
entries.sources: HA 40 (1971) p. 22; Zertal 2008 (MHCS 2) pp. 104–107, 151–153, 191–198; SWP II pp. 237, 240; see entry59_bezek_review.md, source_leads_2026-09-29.md and source_extractions_2026-09-29.md

entries.title: The final Kohlit entry
entries.description: A pit, tomb and opening associated with Kohlit; Lefkovits also reads Janoah.
entries.evidence: North of Tell es-Sultan, Kenyon records Qumran-type Roman graves (Jericho II p. 2, pp. 516–545; III pp. 173–174), a Roman burial in a Bronze Age shaft (D9), later undated quarry pits that cut graves, and a Roman cistern with “Herodian” lamps toward Kh. el-Mefjar (N.S.1, II pp. 539–544).
entries.caution: Koḥlit is unidentified; Tell es-Sultan is Puech’s hypothesis. No pit with tombs at its mouth is recorded, and the strip just north of the tell was never searched (Kenyon II p. 169). In the registered Koḥlit rarity count its pit is UNKNOWN; it is one of 23 units meeting two of three conditions (after the source-2 addendum), and none meets all three.
entries.period: North-slope graves 1st c. CE by grave-type comparison only; quarry pits undated; the tell itself EB only in WBADB
entries.sources: Phase 3 site index; Phase 2 landmark lexicon
